title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud

header.html: Describe cloud security posture management (CSPM); Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud; Describe security policies and standards; Describe security recommendations; Describe cloud workload protection
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1What Defender for Cloud is

Microsoft Defender for Cloud is a cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) that does two jobs:

Job Name Question it answers
Find and fix weaknesses Cloud security posture management (CSPM) Is my environment configured securely?
Detect and stop threats Cloud workload protection (CWP), delivered by Defender plans Are my workloads under attack right now?

It protects Azure, on-premises servers and other clouds such as AWS and Google Cloud (multicloud).

Exam tip

. CSPM = posture (misconfiguration, recommendations, secure score). Workload protection = threats (alerts and defenses per resource type). Defender for Cloud covers multicloud and hybrid, not Azure only.

2Cloud security posture management (CSPM)

Feature What it does
Secure score A percentage showing how well you follow security recommendations; higher is better
Security recommendations Prioritized, actionable steps to fix weaknesses
Regulatory compliance dashboard Shows how you measure against standards
Asset inventory One view of all resources and their security state
Attack path analysis and cloud security graph Shows how an attacker could reach critical assets (Defender CSPM plan) [Verify live]
Governance rules Assign owners and due dates to recommendations

Free foundational CSPM is included for Azure; Defender CSPM is the paid plan with advanced features. [Verify live]

3Security recommendations

A recommendation tells you what to fix, why, and how. Each shows severity, affected resources and remediation steps, and many offer Quick fix or Fix buttons. Examples: enable MFA for accounts, close management ports on VMs, enable encryption, apply system updates.

Recommendations are generated by security policies and standards that are assessed continuously. Secure score rises as you fix them.

4Security policies and standards

Term Meaning
Security policy A rule about how resources should be configured (built on Azure Policy)
Initiative A group of policies assigned together
Standard A set of controls from a benchmark or regulation
Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB) The default standard, Microsoft's security best practices for Azure and multicloud
Regulatory standards For example ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST SP 800-53, SOC 2 can be added

Exam tip

. Policies and standards define what is expected; recommendations tell you what to do; secure score shows progress. The default standard is the Microsoft cloud security benchmark.

5Cloud workload protection (Defender plans)

Each Defender plan protects a resource type with threat detection and alerts:

Plan Protects
Defender for Servers Virtual machines and servers (Azure, on-premises, other clouds); includes vulnerability assessment and endpoint protection with Defender for Endpoint
Defender for Storage Storage accounts: malware scanning, unusual access
Defender for Databases (SQL, open-source databases, Cosmos DB) Databases: SQL injection and anomalous access
Defender for App Service Web apps
Defender for Key Vault Key vault misuse
Defender for Containers Kubernetes and container images
Defender for Resource Manager Suspicious management operations
Defender for APIs API threats

Key points: plans are enabled per subscription, are paid by resource, and raise security alerts with recommended responses; alerts can be sent to Microsoft Sentinel and the Defender XDR portal. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. "Detect attacks on virtual machines, databases or storage" = a Defender plan (workload protection). "Score and recommendations about configuration" = CSPM.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants a percentage that shows how well its Azure resources follow security recommendations. What is it?

  • ACompliance score in Purview
  • BSecure score
  • CSign-in risk
  • DNSG priority
Show the answer

Answer: B. Secure score in Defender for Cloud measures posture against recommendations.

S2Which Defender for Cloud capability detects an attack on a SQL database?

  • ACloud workload protection with a Defender plan
  • BSecure score, which only shows configuration posture
  • CThe asset inventory of all your resources
  • DSensitivity labels applied to documents
Show the answer

Answer: A. Defender plans provide threat detection for specific workloads such as databases.

S3What is the default security standard in Defender for Cloud?

  • AISO 27001 only, which must be added first
  • BPCI DSS only, which must be added first
  • CGDPR, a regulation that the customer adds afterward
  • DMicrosoft cloud security benchmark
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is the default standard.

S4A team wants guidance on which settings to change to improve security, with severity and remediation steps. Which feature gives this?

  • AAzure Bastion
  • BA Conditional Access policy
  • CSecurity recommendations
  • DAccess reviews
Show the answer

Answer: C. Recommendations are prioritized, actionable remediation guidance.

S5Which statement about Defender for Cloud is true?

  • AIt protects only Azure virtual machines and nothing else
  • BIt is a SIEM only and has no posture features at all
  • CIt manages user passwords for every employee account
  • DIt protects Azure, on-premises and other clouds
Show the answer

Answer: D. Defender for Cloud covers multicloud and hybrid environments.

S6Which term describes a group of policies assigned together?

  • ARecommendation
  • BAlert
  • CInitiative
  • DTenant
Show the answer

Answer: C. An initiative bundles several policies.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does CSPM stand for?

Show the answer

Cloud security posture management.

R2What does secure score show?

Show the answer

How well you follow security recommendations; higher is better.

R3What do Defender plans provide?

Show the answer

Cloud workload protection: threat detection and alerts per resource type.

R4Name the default standard.

Show the answer

Microsoft cloud security benchmark.

R5Which Azure service do Defender for Cloud policies build on?

Show the answer

Azure Policy.

R6Which paid plan adds attack path analysis?

Show the answer

Defender CSPM.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Defender for Cloud CNAPP; CSPM plus cloud workload protection; Azure, on-premises, multicloud
CSPM secure score, recommendations, compliance dashboard, inventory, attack paths (Defender CSPM)
Policies and standards Azure Policy based; initiatives; default Microsoft cloud security benchmark; add ISO, PCI, NIST
Workload protection Defender for Servers, Storage, Databases, App Service, Key Vault, Containers, Resource Manager, APIs
